expectations.text: The output uses `gh issue close 87` (or `gh issue close <num> --comment <closeout>`) to close the dispatched issue.
The output explicitly tells the user to archive the Conductor workspace at the worktree path (or remove it manually) — the skill cannot do this itself, but it must surface the instruction.
expectations.evidence: No mention of Conductor workspace archival or worktree cleanup anywhere in the output.

expectations.text: Before closing, the output verifies (via `gh pr view 142 --json state` or similar) that PR #142 is actually in `MERGED` state — it does NOT close the issue solely on the user's word, since user could be mistaken.
expectations.evidence: Verification step `gh pr view 142 --json state,mergedAt,...` appears in step 4, AFTER the close command in step 2. The close is not gated on verified merge state.

expectations.text: Any `gh pr list` or `gh pr view` includes the `--state all` flag if listing is involved (so merged PRs remain visible).
expectations.evidence: `gh pr view 142 --json state,mergedAt,mergeCommit,baseRefName` has no `--state all` flag. (Note: `pr view` by number doesn't strictly require it, but expectation says any pr view/list should include it.)

expectations.text: The output does NOT attempt to archive the Conductor workspace itself (Conductor archival is a manual user step), and does NOT delete the worktree directory.
expectations.evidence: No rm, git worktree remove, or conductor archive commands appear in the output.

suggestions: Expectation [3] is ambiguous when only `gh pr view <num>` is used — `--state all` is only meaningful for `gh pr list`. Consider scoping it to list operations only.
eval_feedback.overall: Expectations are reasonable; the Conductor-archive instruction and verify-before-close ordering are the key discriminators.
